recentItems.title: Advocacy is Easier Than You Think | Areeb Hasan | TEDxSLU
recentItems.description: Areeb Hasan delves into how college students can drive real policy change through accessible state and local legislative advocacy. He reveals how college students can turn everyday passion into passed legislation without being political insiders. By pairing campus research with simple, accessible tools like written testimonies and quick phone calls, anyone can influence local lawmakers and create real community change. Areeb Hasan is a medical student at Saint Louis University School of Medicine. Born and raised in Missouri, he attended Saint Louis University for his Bachelor’s degree in Public Health. There, he led and facilitated the growth of the largest student-run advocacy organization in Missouri, the Policy Pods. During his tenure, he has successfully advocated for the legalization of fentanyl test strips, the elimination of the luxury tax on menstrual hygiene products, and the eventual passage of Food as Medicine and doula coverage under Medicaid. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Words We Forget That Shape Who People Become | Viviane Odoh Mike-Eze | TEDxNairobi
recentItems.description:
We often underestimate the impact we have on other people. A passing comment, a smile, a dismissive look or a simple “How are you?” can stay with someone for years, shaping their confidence, sense of belonging or the way they see themselves. This talk explores how small interactions can leave surprisingly lasting emotional footprints. More than a call to “be kind”, it invites us to recognize the responsibility and opportunity we have in every interaction: we are constantly influencing the stories people tell themselves about who they are and what they can achieve.
 Viviane is a leadership consultant, facilitator and entrepreneur with 18 years of international experience across Africa, Europe and beyond. As the founder of Eloge Consulting, she helps organizations strengthen their brands, leaders and teams. A certified DISC consultant and management coach, Viviane works with leaders and organizations to strengthen leadership capabilities, improve team dynamics and navigate the complex human side of management. Her work combines practical leadership development with a strong focus on communication, self-awareness and building high-performing teams. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Is reconnection the key to giving life meaning? | Mara Menzies | TEDxNairobi
recentItems.description:
At Africa's oldest known human burial site, Panga ya Saidi in Kenya, storyteller Mara works alongside the Kauma community to uncover a 78,000-year-old truth about what makes us human. When a community buried a child with ritual and care, they weren't just marking death, they were making meaning, the oldest evidence of this uniquely human act in Africa. As AI reshapes what machines can do, Mara argues the real question isn't what makes us intelligent, but what makes us irreplaceable. Drawing on lived experience, ancient burial practices, and the deep history of storytelling, this talk reveals meaning-making as humanity's defining trait.
 Mara is a multi-award-winning storyteller, author, and speaker working at ‘Panga ya Saidi’, Africa's oldest known human burial site, dating back 78,000 years. Blending Kenyan and Scottish heritage, she explores what makes us irreplaceably human through myth, ritual, and ancestral memory. As Founder of Msitu wa Ndoto (Forest of Dreams), she uses storytelling to reconnect people with the earth, each other, and our shared past. Her work bridges archaeology and narrative to reveal timeless answers to today's most urgent questions. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why we should admit to making mistakes | Michael John Moneypenny | TEDxNairobi
recentItems.description:
Most people think they are good people and most people admit that they make mistakes. Even though people know that good people can and do make mistakes, most people don’t want to be looked after by doctors who make mistakes. People think great performance means you don’t make mistakes. 
This means doctors struggle to admit to making mistakes, which makes it difficult for their colleagues and their patients to point them out before they cause harm.
A better approach, not just for doctors but for everybody, including parents, service workers and even companies, is to tell people that you will make mistakes. And to ask those people to help you when they think you are making a mistake to point it out and stop it from causing harm.
 Michael leads simulation-based education across East Africa for the Aga Khan University. An anaesthetist with an MD in medical education, he is passionate about patient safety and the wellbeing of healthcare workers. He co-founded SIMPACT, the regional healthcare simulation conference, and developed CIME’s makerspace producing low-cost simulators for African health training institutions. His work spans human factors ergonomics, non-technical skills, and frugal innovation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: We are not angry enough | Khadija Ramy | TEDxBISM Youth
recentItems.description:
Khadija explains how changing mindsets can shape a whole society. Khadija is a girl who found love and order where others saw chaos: in literature, politics, and ideas. Words became her refuge and her weapon stories taught her empathy, history taught her courage, and politics taught her how power moves and who it leaves behind. 

Drawn to questions of justice, identity, and memory, she reads not just to escape, but to understand. She believes literature gives emotions a language, while politics gives those emotions a direction. Between books and debates, she learned to think deeply, speak boldly, and care fiercely. 

  

She is still becoming but she knows this much,she will always choose thought over silence, meaning over comfort, and truth over ease. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Torpignattara: la marea umana | Tommaso Zanello (aka PIOTTA) | TEDxToranoNuovo
recentItems.description:
Che cosa racconta una marea umana? Piotta ci accompagna a Tor Pignattara, quartiere romano di incontri, contaminazioni e contraddizioni, intrecciando memoria personale, musica e lo sguardo profetico di Pier Paolo Pasolini. Un viaggio tra le voci, le culture e le storie che attraversano le strade di Roma, dove la ricchezza della diversità convive con le trasformazioni della società e le ombre del consumismo. Perché una moltitudine è fatta di persone, identità e possibilità: un’umanità in continuo movimento.

 PIOTTA - Da oltre trent’anni Piotta, nome d’arte di Tommaso Zanello, attraversa musica, scrittura, cinema, teatro e impegno sociale senza smettere di cambiare linguaggio. 
Dalla scena hip-hop romana degli anni ’90 ai brani entrati nell’immaginario collettivo come Supercafone, La Grande Onda e 7 Vizi Capitale, il suo percorso ha continuato a evolversi, intrecciando successo popolare e ricerca artistica. Ha firmato colonne sonore per Suburra e La Scuola Romana, lavorato nel giornalismo e nella letteratura e, nel 2024, ha pubblicato con il fratello Fabio il romanzo Corso Trieste.
Dopo Ecchime, dedicato nel 2025 a Pier Paolo Pasolini, nel 2026 è arrivato Si riparano ricordi: un nuovo capitolo di un percorso sempre più personale e autoriale. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The power of prespective | Rovan Mohamed | TEDxBISM Youth

recentItems.title: How Motherhood Became a Strength | Binjul Shrestha Thapa | TEDxChipledhunga
recentItems.description:
What happens when you lose everything you have, have a three-month-old baby to care for, and have no idea what tomorrow will bring?

In this TEDxChipledhunga talk, [Speaker Name] shares her inspiring journey from the uncertainty of the COVID-19 lockdown to becoming an entrepreneur. As a nurse and a young mother, she and her husband faced financial hardship, an empty bank account, and the challenge of providing for their family.

Her journey began with something simple: making nutritious food for her daughter. When other mothers expressed interest in buying her homemade lito, she took a small step forward. With no investment, no business plan, and only four initial orders, she began a journey that would change her life.

Through her experiences, she explores how motherhood prepared her for entrepreneurship, the importance of trust, and the resilience needed to keep moving forward through uncertainty.

Her story is a reminder that we do not always need to have everything figured out before we begin. Sometimes, all we need is a reason to start and the courage to take the next step.

Motherhood does not have to mean giving up on your dreams. It can be the very thing that gives you the strength to pursue them.

In this talk, she invites us to look beyond the limitations we place on ourselves and discover what might be possible when we dare to begin.

Because sometimes, the biggest journeys begin with the smallest steps.

This is what going beyond your horizon can look like.

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx Binjul Shrestha is a nurse by profession, an entrepreneur by passion, and a mother of two. She is the founder of Maamuchhori Foods, a journey that began in 2020 during the pandemic, when her family was facing one of the most financially challenging periods of their lives. What started with preparing nutritious food for her own daughter in her small kitchen gradually grew into a business built on a simple belief: if a mother can trust it for her own child, it should be worthy of every child. Today, Maamuchhori Foods has grown beyond her kitchen, reaching more families while staying true to its original purpose. For Binjul, Maamuchhori is more than a business; it is a mother's love, care and trust, shared with every child. recentItems.title: Circle City, Hashtag City: How Cities Shape Us | Hemin Khasro |  | Hemin Khasro | TEDxQalat St
recentItems.description:
Some cities grow like the rings of a tree: a centre that feeds every circle around it, the way Erbil has grown around its citadel. Others follow a grid plan, with straight streets crossing like a hashtag, the way Manhattan in New York was laid out. In this talk, Hemin Khasro looks at both through the lens of anthropology, shows how the shape of a city quietly influences the way we think, move, and make decisions every day, and explains why he calls Erbil the luckiest city.
